cues.en: Instructor: In this video, I'm going to talk about probability functions and also the difference between probability mass function and a probability density function.
cues.zh: 講師：這部影片要談機率函數，以及機率質量函數和機率密度函數的差異。

cues.en: And along the way, you will also learn more about the exact definition of probabilities.
cues.zh: 過程中也會更深入了解機率的精確定義。

cues.en: Okay, so let's start just by defining three important terms.
cues.zh: 先定義三個重要術語。

cues.en: So this one we already know, a probability is the chance that a specific event will occur.
cues.zh: 這個已經知道了，機率就是特定事件發生的可能性。

cues.en: So that's a probability.
cues.zh: 這就是機率。

cues.en: Then we have a probability mass and a probability density.
cues.zh: 接著是機率質量與機率密度。

cues.en: These are both functions.
cues.zh: 它們都是函數。

cues.en: So a probability mass function is a function that describes probabilities for a set of exclusive discrete events.
cues.zh: 機率質量函數，是描述一組互斥離散事件之機率的函數。

cues.en: So a probability mass function describes probabilities for discrete events.
cues.zh: 所以，機率質量函數描述離散事件的機率。

cues.en: And a probability density function is a function that describes probabilities for exclusive continuous events.
cues.zh: 機率密度函數，則是描述互斥連續事件之機率的函數。

cues.en: So the important distinction between probability mass and probability density is whether the events are discrete or whether they are continuous.
cues.zh: 因此，機率質量和機率密度的重要差異，在於事件是離散還是連續。

cues.en: Okay, so now I'm going to take a few moments, so the rest of this lecture basically, to explain the general concept of a probability function, and then more clearly discuss the distinction
cues.zh: 接下來花一點時間，基本上是這堂課剩下的時間，解釋機率函數的一般概念，再更清楚地討論

cues.en: between a mass and a density.
cues.zh: 質量和密度的差異。

cues.en: All right, so here we have a whole bunch of mathy things.
cues.zh: 這裡有一大堆數學內容。

cues.en: I'm going to go through all of these terms and each of these statements one at a time.
cues.zh: 我會逐一說明所有術語和每個陳述。

cues.en: So first, a few definitions.
cues.zh: 先給幾個定義。

cues.en: So capital green X here is all of the values of a variable.
cues.zh: 這裡綠色的大寫 X，表示某個變數的所有值。

cues.en: So let's say we are doing some research about, I don't know, what TV show people are watching right now online.
cues.zh: 假設我們在研究，人們目前在網路上看什麼影集。

cues.en: So then X, big X, green big X would be the set of all TV shows in our list that we are considering.
cues.zh: 那麼綠色大寫 X，就是我們考慮的清單中，所有影集組成的集合。

cues.en: Maybe, you know, we have a list of, let's say, 50 of the most popular shows right now.
cues.zh: 也許列出目前最熱門的 50 部影集。

cues.en: So that's big X, that's all of the values in a set.
cues.zh: 這就是大寫 X，也就是集合中的所有值。

cues.en: And then we have little blue X here, and that is the unique values that are contained within big X.
cues.zh: 這裡還有藍色小寫 x，表示大寫 X 所包含的不重複數值。

cues.en: So X would be, you know, "Game of Thrones," for example, would be one of the values of the TV shows, the set of TV shows under consideration.
cues.zh: 例如，《權力遊戲》就是所考慮影集集合中的一個值。

cues.en: So this right here is our statement of a probability function.
cues.zh: 這裡就是機率函數的陳述。

cues.en: So a probability function is a function of a variable X that is defined by the probability of that event X occurring given the set of X.
cues.zh: 機率函數是變數 x 的函數，定義為在給定集合 X 下，事件 x 發生的機率。

cues.en: So the function is simply defined by the probability of each event occurring, that's really all this says.
cues.zh: 所以函數只是由每個事件發生的機率定義，這句話表達的就是如此。

cues.en: And then we have this line, and this is actually not really a whole lot different from this.
cues.zh: 接著這一行，其實和這裡沒有太大不同。

cues.en: This is just clarifying that each individual element of this function is equal to the probability of that event occurring.
cues.zh: 只是釐清，這個函數的每個個別元素，等於那個事件發生的機率。

cues.en: So the probability of, you know, X sub i, watching the "Game of Thrones," so the value of the probability function for "Game of Thrones" is equal to the probability
cues.zh: 例如 x 下標 i，也就是觀看《權力遊戲》，機率函數對《權力遊戲》的值，就等於

cues.en: that people are watching that particular TV show out of this set of TV shows.
cues.zh: 人們在這組影集中，觀看這部特定影集的機率。

cues.en: Okay, and then we have all these substatements here, and they all start with s.t., which means such that, so these are like conditionals on this definition here.
cues.zh: 接著有這些附加陳述，都以 s.t. 開頭，代表 such that，也就是對這個定義附加的條件。

cues.en: So the first such that is that probabilities must be non-negative.
cues.zh: 第一個條件是，機率必須非負。

cues.en: So all of these probabilities have to be greater than or equal to zero.
cues.zh: 所以所有機率都必須大於或等於 0。

cues.en: They can be zero, of course, we can say no one is watching "Game of Thrones" anymore.
cues.zh: 當然可以是 0，例如可以說，已經沒有人看《權力遊戲》了。

cues.en: Anyone who ever wants to see "Game of Thrones" is already done watching it and there's no new viewers, so the probability could be zero but it can't be less than zero.
cues.zh: 所有想看的人都已經看完，而且沒有新觀眾，所以機率可以為 0，但不能小於 0。

cues.en: We can't say the probability of watching "Game of Thrones" is minus 10%, that doesn't make any sense.
cues.zh: 不能說觀看《權力遊戲》的機率是 −10%，那沒有意義。

cues.en: Okay, and then this next statement says that events must be exclusive.
cues.zh: 下一個陳述說，事件必須互斥。

cues.en: So basically this is saying that the probability when we're considering X sub i, the probability of X sub i, or the function value of X sub i,
cues.zh: 基本上，在考慮 x 下標 i，也就是 xᵢ 的機率或函數值時，

cues.en: must be zero for all other values of X that are not equal to X sub i.
cues.zh: 對所有不等於 xᵢ 的其他 x 值，這個值必須為 0。

cues.en: So if you are watching "Game of Thrones" right now, you're not simultaneously watching any other TV show, not even "Futurama."
cues.zh: 所以如果你現在看《權力遊戲》，就不會同時看其他影集，連《飛出個未來》也不行。

cues.en: So there is some aspect of exclusivity.
cues.zh: 這裡有互斥性。

cues.en: And then the final condition that we have here is that the sum of all probabilities must equal to one.
cues.zh: 最後一個條件是，所有機率的總和必須等於 1。

cues.en: So all the Xis, the probabilities of all the different shows together equals exactly one.
cues.zh: 所有不同影集的機率，加起來恰好等於 1。

cues.en: And of course, this could also be 100 if you are thinking about these probabilities in terms of percent.
cues.zh: 如果用百分比思考，當然也可以是 100。

cues.en: Okay, so these are the characteristics of probability functions in general.
cues.zh: 這些就是一般機率函數的特性。

cues.en: Now we need to distinguish between two families of probability functions, probability mass functions and probability density functions.
cues.zh: 現在必須區分兩大類機率函數：機率質量函數，以及機率密度函數。

cues.en: So let's start with probability mass functions.
cues.zh: 先從機率質量函數開始。

cues.en: Remember I defined this before as being for discrete events.
cues.zh: 記得，前面定義它適用於離散事件。

cues.en: So discrete events are all sorts of things that I've already introduced you to.
cues.zh: 離散事件包含之前介紹的各種情況。

cues.en: So picking one specific card out of a deck of cards, picking out a marble from a jar, flipping a coin, rolling a die, these are all discrete events.
cues.zh: 從一副牌抽出特定的一張、從罐子抽彈珠、擲硬幣、擲骰子，都是離散事件。

cues.en: Probability mass functions have associated visualizations that must be in a bar plot or in a histogram, but they look something like this.
cues.zh: 機率質量函數對應的視覺化，必須是長條圖或直方圖，看起來像這樣。

cues.en: These are discrete events, so they have to be separated from each other like this.
cues.zh: 這些是離散事件，所以必須像這樣彼此分開。

cues.en: So here's a question for you, are you allowed to draw lines between these successive bars or these successive stems here?
cues.zh: 問你一個問題，可以在相鄰長條或這些相鄰豎線之間畫線嗎？

cues.en: So could you draw something like this?
cues.zh: 可以畫成這樣嗎？

cues.en: Well, this is something I discussed earlier towards the end of this section on visualization, and the answer is you shouldn't really do it.
cues.zh: 我在資料視覺化那一章的最後談過，答案是，其實不應該這樣做。

cues.en: Sometimes for some types of data it can be possible.
cues.zh: 有時對某些資料類型，可能可以。

cues.en: What you are saying when you draw a line here, let's imagine this is the probability of rolling a die and getting a particular number.
cues.zh: 假設這是擲骰子得到某個數字的機率，當你在這裡畫線，表示的是什麼？

cues.en: Maybe it's a loaded die, it's an unfair die.
cues.zh: 也許是動過手腳、不公平的骰子。

cues.en: So this would be the probability of rolling a one, this would be the probability of rolling a two.
cues.zh: 這裡是擲出 1 的機率，這裡是擲出 2 的機率。

cues.en: Now, when you draw a line between these two points like this, what you are implicitly stating is that the probability
cues.zh: 在這兩點之間畫線，就隱含地表示，

cues.en: of rolling a 1.5 is whatever this value is here.
cues.zh: 擲出 1.5 的機率，是這裡的這個值。

cues.en: Now that doesn't make any sense of course, you can't roll a 1.5.
cues.zh: 但這當然沒有意義，不可能擲出 1.5。

cues.en: So really you shouldn't draw lines in between these different events.
cues.zh: 所以其實不應該在這些不同事件之間畫線。

cues.en: That said, you know, I also mentioned that lines can sometimes be acceptable if the probability mass function is really tightly sampled or if you have several different probability distributions
cues.zh: 話雖如此，我也提過，如果機率質量函數的取樣非常密集，或有好幾種不同機率分布，

cues.en: that you're trying to visualize on the same graph, then lines can be okay for numeric data under some circumstances.
cues.zh: 想放在同一張圖呈現，那麼在某些情況下，數值資料使用線條可以接受。

cues.en: So the default should be that probability mass functions really should be drawn with bars or with stem plots or something, you know, discontinuous, and lines can be okay in some cases.
cues.zh: 所以，預設應該使用長條、豎線圖，或某種不連續的呈現方式來畫機率質量函數，但有些情況可以畫線。

cues.en: Okay, so probability mass is for discrete events.
cues.zh: 好，機率質量適用於離散事件。

cues.en: A probability density is a function for continuous events.
cues.zh: 機率密度則是連續事件的函數。

cues.en: And here we are thinking about events that are not countable because they're sort of arbitrarily precise.
cues.zh: 這裡考慮的事件不可數，因為可以有任意精度。

cues.en: And I've already given some examples with height.
cues.zh: 之前已經舉過身高的例子。

cues.en: Here's another example with age, you know, no one is really, you're not 24 years old.
cues.zh: 這裡再舉年齡，例如其實沒有人真正恰好是 24 歲。

cues.en: You know, we say colloquially that you're 24 years old, but that really means that you are in between your 25th and 24th birthday, so we actually discretized that.
cues.zh: 日常會說你 24 歲，但真正的意思是，你在第 24 和第 25 次生日之間，所以其實已經離散化。

cues.en: And in fact your true age is, you know, 24.237900, you know, whatever, it's going to go on to infinity
cues.zh: 真正年齡是 24.237900 等等，會一直延伸下去，

cues.en: until we discretized time to Planck scale.
cues.zh: 直到把時間離散化到普朗克尺度。

cues.en: Now money is an interesting case because we generally just break down money to depending on what currency you're coming from, but you know, many currencies would have two levels
cues.zh: 金錢是有趣的情況，因為通常依貨幣而定，很多貨幣會把金額分到

cues.en: of precision, two orders of precision after the decimal point.
cues.zh: 小數點後兩位的精度。

cues.en: But still, we often think about money as a continuous event and we discretized it.
cues.zh: 但我們仍經常把金錢想成連續事件，再將它離散化。

cues.en: So we don't say, "what is the probability of someone having a salary of $61,23.28 per year?"
cues.zh: 所以不會問：「某人的年薪恰好為 $61,23.28 的機率是多少？」

cues.en: Instead we say, you know, "The probability of discretizing this salary amount to," let's say, "increments of $10,000."
cues.zh: 而是說，把薪資金額離散化成，例如每 1 萬美元一個區間，再談機率。

cues.en: And here I have distance, it's also an example of a continuous event.
cues.zh: 這裡還有距離，也是連續事件的例子。

cues.en: So it turns out that if you wanted to walk from Amsterdam to Ho Chi Minh City in Vietnam, turns out that that is 12,131 kilometers.
cues.zh: 如果想從阿姆斯特丹走到越南胡志明市，距離是 12,131 公里。

cues.en: It would take 2,460 hours, which as it turns out is 102.5 days,
cues.zh: 需要 2460 小時，算起來是 102.5 天，

cues.en: which as it turns out is approximately three and a half months.
cues.zh: 大約三個半月。

cues.en: So it would take three and a half months without sleeping, without stopping to take a pee break or anything.
cues.zh: 所以三個半月不能睡覺，不能停下來上廁所，什麼都不能停。

cues.en: You would take three and a half months to walk from Amsterdam to Vietnam, why anyone would want to do that I have no idea because you can just fly, okay?
cues.zh: 從阿姆斯特丹走到越南要三個半月，我不知道為什麼有人想這樣做，因為可以搭飛機，好嗎？

cues.en: Anyway, the point was that the distance from Amsterdam to Vietnam is not 12,131 kilometers exactly.
cues.zh: 總之，重點是阿姆斯特丹到越南的距離，不會恰好就是 12,131 公里。

cues.en: You know, there's going to be meters and centimeters and you know, millimeters all the way down to picometers.
cues.zh: 還會有公尺、公分、毫米，一路到皮米。

cues.en: You can eventually get all the way to Planck scale.
cues.zh: 最後甚至可以到普朗克尺度。

cues.en: So instead for convenience, we would talk about probabilities with distances by discretizing them.
cues.zh: 所以為了方便，談距離的機率時會先將它離散化。

cues.en: Okay, anyway, these are all examples of continuous phenomenon.
cues.zh: 總之，這些都是連續現象的例子。

cues.en: So these get probability density functions and probability density functions are smooth and they can be evaluated at lots of different values.
cues.zh: 因此會用機率密度函數，而機率密度函數是平滑的，可以在很多不同數值上求值。

cues.en: Now, I mentioned in the first video of this section that you cannot compute a probability for a continuous event like height.
cues.zh: 本章第一部影片提過，不能為身高這類連續事件直接計算單點機率。

cues.en: Instead, you can only compute probability for a range of events.
cues.zh: 只能計算一段事件範圍的機率。

cues.en: So for example, we can say what is the probability of a king penguin being between this height and this height?
cues.zh: 例如，國王企鵝身高介於這個值和這個值之間的機率是多少？

cues.en: So between these two boundaries.
cues.zh: 也就是介於這兩個邊界之間。

cues.en: So how do you go about computing that probability?
cues.zh: 該如何計算這個機率？

cues.en: Well, you've probably guessed it, we have to use some calculus.
cues.zh: 你大概猜到了，必須使用微積分。

cues.en: We would say the probability of that event, I guess now I'm using a slightly different X than a few slides ago, so my apologies for the slightly confusing notation,
cues.zh: 這個事件的機率，這裡使用的 X 和前幾張投影片稍有不同，抱歉記號有點混淆，

cues.en: but I think you get the idea.
cues.zh: 但我想你能理解。

cues.en: So the probability of a certain value of X being between a and b is equal to the integral, so you have to compute the definite integral
cues.zh: 某個 X 值介於 a 和 b 之間的機率，等於積分，也就是計算

cues.en: between these two boundaries of the probability function and then dx here.
cues.zh: 這個機率函數在兩個邊界之間的定積分，這裡還有 dx。

cues.en: Because we have infinitesimal discretization of this function.
cues.zh: 因為對這個函數進行無窮小的離散化。

cues.en: So another thing you can do with probability densities is compute the probability of, for example, a penguin being up to a certain height.
cues.zh: 機率密度還能用來計算，例如企鵝身高不超過某個值的機率。

cues.en: So what is the probability that a penguin is anywhere between, you know, like zero centimeters and 63.7210 centimeters?
cues.zh: 也就是企鵝身高介於 0 公分到 63.7210 公分之間的機率是多少？

cues.en: So that's also something we can compute using calculus.
cues.zh: 這也可以用微積分計算。

cues.en: So in this video I gave you a more formal definition of a probability function, and I defined and described the differences between a probability mass function,
cues.zh: 這部影片給出了機率函數較正式的定義，也定義並說明了機率質量函數，

cues.en: which is four discrete variables, and a probability density function, which is for continuous variables.
cues.zh: 也就是適用於離散變數的函數，以及適用於連續變數的機率密度函數之間的差異。

cues.en: Now, the last thing I want to say here is that if you are studying probability theory and statistics from a more kind of formal mathematical perspective,
cues.zh: 最後想說，如果從比較正式的數學角度研究機率理論和統計，

cues.en: then you're going to be dealing a lot with probability density functions.
cues.zh: 就會大量處理機率密度函數。

cues.en: You're going to be applying principles of calculus, doing a lot of integration problems and so on.
cues.zh: 會應用微積分原理，進行很多積分題目等等。

cues.en: But if you are approaching calculus from a more applied perspective, you're interested in working with probabilities and statistics for empirical datasets in, you know,
cues.zh: 但如果從比較應用的角度切入微積分，想在實驗資料集上使用機率與統計，例如

cues.en: in science, in medicine, in machine learning, deep learning and so on, then nearly all the time, possibly all the time, certainly most of the time,
cues.zh: 科學、醫學、機器學習、深度學習等等，那麼幾乎所有時候，也許所有時候，至少肯定是大部分時候，

cues.en: you are only going to be working with probability masses and not probability densities.
cues.zh: 只會處理機率質量，而不是機率密度。

cues.en: And that's because, well, first of all, computers can't actually really represent a density because they have limited precision.
cues.zh: 原因首先是，電腦其實無法真正表示密度，因為精度有限。

cues.en: But also in practice, in statistics and applied statistics, we generally always discretized all of our continuous variables.
cues.zh: 此外，在統計與應用統計實務中，通常總是會把所有連續變數離散化。

cues.en: And so we are really always, pretty much always working with probability mass functions.
cues.zh: 所以實際上一直，幾乎一直，都在處理機率質量函數。
